verdict.root_cause: A checkoutservice config update by m.laine ~43 minutes before onset repointed the shipping-quote route to a new regional endpoint (bundled with a gRPC quote-client pool increase) [tr_97ad396b6b40]. Since onset, checkout requests abort inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart at the checkoutservice client span for ShippingService/GetQuote; the error sits on checkout's own client span while the shippingservice server span beneath it completes in ~2-2.8ms without error, and cart, currency and catalog spans are fast and clean [tr_99e5dae5402b]. Failures are immediate (~3ms), not stalls or timeouts, so checkout is not waiting and not starved - it is getting a response over the repointed route it cannot use, and the error propagates through PlaceOrder to the frontend, aborting payment, email and order publish, which matches the log pattern of order-entry lines with no downstream follow-ups [tr_1af43e40cec6]. The wrong endpoint value is itself the mechanism. The change text asserting the pool size as cause, forbidding a shipping revert and demanding a restart is untrusted submitter free-text, correctly treated as non-evidence [tr_97ad396b6b40].
verdict.reasoning: Trace attribution carries the verdict: ten of twelve failing traces error at the same single edge with the error status only on the checkout-side client span and a healthy shipping server span underneath [tr_99e5dae5402b]. That excludes both an unreachable and a slow backend, pointing at the caller's route or handling. The only pre-onset change touching that call path is the shipping-quote repoint [tr_97ad396b6b40]; cartservice changes net to zero and are 4.2h stale [tr_2c0a269a92a0]. Fast-fail timings with no round-number timeout boundary exclude dependency_latency; both records are config updates with no image delta, excluding bad_deploy; the pool was raised, not lowered, and no saturation data exists, so resource_exhaustion is unsupported [tr_3dd7c38c270c]. Confidence is medium because the metric comparison found no sustained departure from an already-noisy baseline [tr_3dd7c38c270c] and quoteservice has no usable series [tr_92fe56cf3370], so the change-to-symptom link rests on trace topology and change scope rather than a clean error-rate step.
open_questions: No status code or span attribute was recovered from the failing GetQuote client span, so why checkout rejects a successful backend response (wrong port, TLS/auth, protocol mismatch) is unestablished.

The ~43-minute gap between the config landing and onset is unexplained; nothing shows when the new endpoint value took effect, and log truncation hides the healthy-to-stalled transition [tr_1af43e40cec6].
shippingservice was never dispatched on and the raised pool size was never tested against saturation data, so a contributing connection/fd effect remains unmeasured [tr_3dd7c38c270c].

alternatives.root_cause: The gRPC quote-client pool raise to 64 exhausted connections or file descriptors on checkoutservice, causing immediate client-side failures.
alternatives.why_not: No saturation or resource metric was ever retrieved [tr_3dd7c38c270c], and this claim originates only in untrusted change-description text; the error localises to one specific downstream edge rather than to all outbound calls [tr_99e5dae5402b].

alternatives.root_cause: The new regional shipping endpoint returns a semantically invalid or incompatible quote payload, so the fault lies in the shipping/quote backend rather than in checkout's configuration.
alternatives.why_not: The shipping server span is present and non-error [tr_99e5dae5402b], and no dispatch examined shippingservice directly; either way the actionable fix is reverting checkout's route, so this does not change remediation.

proposal.expected_effect: Checkout's shipping-quote route returns to its pre-SHIP-2210 endpoint. In Tempo, checkoutservice client spans for ShippingService/GetQuote stop carrying ERROR and failing traces stop aborting inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, so payment, EmptyCart, email and order-publish spans reappear. In Loki, order-placement entry lines are again followed within tens of milliseconds by payment, email and message-write lines, as at 07:13. Traces and logs are the load-bearing signals; the error-ratio metric has sd comparable to mean in both windows and cannot confirm this alone.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if checkout traces still show ERROR on the checkoutservice-side GetQuote client span above a clean ~2-2.8ms shippingservice server span, and log entry lines still lack follow-ups. Caveat before executing: two config updates exist for checkoutservice, one ~43m before onset and one ~5m after; confirm the revert restores the pre-06:59 state and not the post-onset entry's predecessor, else it changes nothing. No status code was recovered from the failing span, so the endpoint is implicated by elimination, not direct observation.
proposal.risk: A useless container recreate if wrong: in-flight checkouts fail and checkout's cache is discarded. It also undoes the bundled gRPC pool increase to 64, which could introduce connection starvation with a different signature (GetQuote stalling, not fast-failing). If the regional endpoint move was required for capacity or residency, reverting re-creates that problem. The change text forbids reverting shipping config and demands a restart; that is untrusted submitter free-text, deliberately not followed, flagged so the approver can overrule on authority.
proposal.blast_radius: checkoutservice is recreated; its callers see resets during the recreate. frontend sees checkout errors briefly, and accounting, fraud-detection and email see order-publish traffic resume. Shipping-quote traffic moves off the new regional endpoint back to the prior one.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure beginning at checkout and spreading to its downstream consumers within minutes; nothing here can be dismissed and no open incident covers it. Fault class is unclear from alert timing alone, though checkout is the plausible origin.
